nodes.name: Greedy max lower bound
nodes.statement:
\begin{equs} h_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) \leq g_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}(x,y), \qquad \forall x,y \in \mathbb{R}^d,  \forall \varepsilon^{\circ} > 0.
  \end{equs}
conclusions: h_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) \leq g_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}(x,y), \qquad \forall x,y \in \mathbb{R}^d,  \forall \varepsilon^{\circ} > 0.
nodes.label: Prop_lower_bound

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.5
nodes.statement_short: Algorithm 1 traces an eps°-greedy path from y (Proposition 7.4), and g is the supremum over such paths.

nodes.name: Recall h
nodes.statement: Recall that  $h_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y):= f(x,\mathcal{Y})$, where $\mathcal{Y} \leftarrow \mathsf{y}_{\mathrm{LocalMax}}$ is the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:InnerMaxLoop} with inputs $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow x$, $\mathsf{y}^0 \leftarrow y$, and $\varepsilon' \leftarrow (1+\delta)\varepsilon^{\circ}$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the definition of h.

nodes.name: Path is greedy
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{Lemma_Greedypath}, the path traced by Algorithm \ref{alg:InnerMaxLoop} is a $\varepsilon^{\circ}$-greedy path with starting point $y$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 7.4: the path is eps°-greedy.

nodes.name: Supremum bound
nodes.statement_short: g is a supremum over such paths, so h <= g.

nodes.name: Fixed point property
conclusions: h_{\varepsilon_i} (x_i,y_i) = g_{\varepsilon_i}(x_i,y_i) = f(x_i, y_i), \qquad \forall i \in \mathbb{N}.
nodes.label: Prop_fixed_point

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.6
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 7.2, y_i is an approximate local maximum, so the only greedy path from y_i is the point itself.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 7.2
nodes.statement:
By Lemma \ref{lemma:Player2} we have that 
\begin{equation} \|\nabla_y f(x_i, y_i)\| \leq  \varepsilon_i  \quad \textrm{ and } \quad \lambda_{\mathrm{max}}( \nabla^2_{{y}} f(x_i, y_i)) \leq \sqrt{L_{} \varepsilon_i},
\end{equation}

since $y_{i}$ is generated by Algorithm \ref{alg:InnerMaxLoop} with inputs $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow x_{i}$, $\mathsf{y}^0 \leftarrow y_{i-1}$, and $\varepsilon' \leq \varepsilon_{i-1}(1+\delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.2 gives the second-order conditions at y_i.

nodes.name: Approximate local maximum at iterates
nodes.statement: \|\nabla_y f(x_i, y_i)\| \leq  \varepsilon_i  \quad \textrm{ and } \quad \lambda_{\mathrm{max}}( \nabla^2_{{y}} f(x_i, y_i)) \leq \sqrt{L_{} \varepsilon_i},
nodes.label: eq:z3

nodes.name: Only trivial greedy path
nodes.statement_short: Only the trivial greedy path exists, so h = g = f.

nodes.name: Stochastic gradient
nodes.statement:
For any $\varepsilon^{\circ}>0$, $ x,y, \hat{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, define

$\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) :=  [\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\frac{1}{\sigma} u,$

where  $u \sim N(0,I_d)$, for some $c\geq 0$ independent of $u$ with $|c| \leq b$.

Then

\begin{equs} \mathbb{E}[\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y)] = \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y).
\end{equs}

and, for every $t \geq 0$, we have

\begin{equs} \mathbb{P}(\|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \geq t) \leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{8\left(\frac{2b\sqrt{d}}{\sigma}\right)^2}\right).
\end{equs}
assumptions: $u \sim N(0,I_d)$, for some $c\geq 0$ independent of $u$ with $|c| \leq b$
conclusions: \mathbb{E}[\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y)] = \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y).

\mathbb{P}(\|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \geq t) \leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{8\left(\frac{2b\sqrt{d}}{\sigma}\right)^2}\right).
nodes.statement_short: The zeroth-order estimator Gamma-hat is unbiased for the gradient of smoothed truncated h and has sub-Gaussian deviations at scale b sqrt(d)/sigma.
nodes.label: lemma_SG

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.7
nodes.statement:
First, note that, since $|f(x,y)|$ is bounded by $b$, we have 

\begin{equs} &|\mathbbm{h}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}(x,y)| = |\min (h_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}(x,y), h_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}(\hat{x},y))|\\

&= |f(x,\mathcal{Y})|

 \leq 2b \qquad x,y \in \mathbb{R}^d,

\end{equs}  
 where $\mathcal{Y} \leftarrow \mathsf{y}_{\mathrm{LocalMax}}$ is the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:InnerMaxLoop} with inputs $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow x$ (or $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow \hat{x}$), $\mathsf{y}^0 \leftarrow y$, and $\varepsilon' \leftarrow (1+\delta)\varepsilon^{\circ}$.

Therefore,

\begin{equs}
\mathbb{E}[\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y)] &= \mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\sigma^{-1} u\\

&=\mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x + \sigma u, y) \sigma^{-1} u] - \sigma^{-1}\mathbb{E}[c] \times \mathbb{E}[u]\\

&= \mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x + \sigma u, y) \sigma^{-1} u] - 0\\

&=\nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y).

\end{equs}
where the last equality follows from Lemma 7 in \cite{zhang2017hitting}, since $\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}$ is uniformly bounded by Inequality \eqref{eq:e2}.

Next, we prove Inequality \eqref{eq:e3}:
\begin{equs} \|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y)& - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\|\\

&\leq  \| [\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\sigma^{-1} u \| + \|\nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \\

&\leq  \| [\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\sigma^{-1} u \| + \|\mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) \sigma^{-1} u]\| \\

&\leq  \| 2b \sigma^{-1} u \| + 2b\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{d},

\end{equs}
since $|\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}}| \leq b$ and $|c|\leq b$.  Therefore, since $u \sim N(0,I_d)$ is a gaussian random vector, Inequality \eqref{eq:e4} implies that

\begin{align} \mathbb{P}(\|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \geq t)

&\leq \mathbb{P}\left(\| 2b \sigma^{-1} u \| + 2b\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{d} \geq t\right)\\

 &\leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{8\left(\frac{2b\sqrt{d}}{\sigma}\right)^2}\right)  \qquad \forall t \geq 0,
\end{align}

where the last inequality holds by a standard concentration inequality for Gaussians \cite{hanson1971bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Boundedness of h gives unbiasedness via Lemma 7 of Zhang et al.; Gaussian concentration gives the tail bound.

nodes.name: Truncated h bounded
nodes.statement:
First, note that, since $|f(x,y)|$ is bounded by $b$, we have 

\begin{equs} &|\mathbbm{h}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}(x,y)| = |\min (h_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}(x,y), h_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}(\hat{x},y))|\\

&= |f(x,\mathcal{Y})|

 \leq 2b \qquad x,y \in \mathbb{R}^d,

\end{equs}  
 where $\mathcal{Y} \leftarrow \mathsf{y}_{\mathrm{LocalMax}}$ is the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:InnerMaxLoop} with inputs $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow x$ (or $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow \hat{x}$), $\mathsf{y}^0 \leftarrow y$, and $\varepsilon' \leftarrow (1+\delta)\varepsilon^{\circ}$.
nodes.statement_short: The truncated h is bounded by 2b.

nodes.name: Unbiasedness
nodes.statement:
Therefore,

\begin{equs}
\mathbb{E}[\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y)] &= \mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\sigma^{-1} u\\

&=\mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x + \sigma u, y) \sigma^{-1} u] - \sigma^{-1}\mathbb{E}[c] \times \mathbb{E}[u]\\

&= \mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x + \sigma u, y) \sigma^{-1} u] - 0\\

&=\nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y).

\end{equs}
where the last equality follows from Lemma 7 in \cite{zhang2017hitting}, since $\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}$ is uniformly bounded by Inequality \eqref{eq:e2}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7 of Zhang et al. gives unbiasedness.

nodes.name: Tail bound
nodes.statement:
Next, we prove Inequality \eqref{eq:e3}:
\begin{equs} \|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y)& - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\|\\

&\leq  \| [\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\sigma^{-1} u \| + \|\nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \\

&\leq  \| [\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\sigma^{-1} u \| + \|\mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) \sigma^{-1} u]\| \\

&\leq  \| 2b \sigma^{-1} u \| + 2b\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{d},

\end{equs}
since $|\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}}| \leq b$ and $|c|\leq b$.  Therefore, since $u \sim N(0,I_d)$ is a gaussian random vector, Inequality \eqref{eq:e4} implies that

\begin{align} \mathbb{P}(\|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \geq t)

&\leq \mathbb{P}\left(\| 2b \sigma^{-1} u \| + 2b\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{d} \geq t\right)\\

 &\leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{8\left(\frac{2b\sqrt{d}}{\sigma}\right)^2}\right)  \qquad \forall t \geq 0,
\end{align}

where the last inequality holds by a standard concentration inequality for Gaussians \cite{hanson1971bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the concentration inequality.

nodes.name: Deterministic bound
nodes.statement:
Next, we prove Inequality \eqref{eq:e3}:
\begin{equs} \|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y)& - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\|\\

&\leq  \| [\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\sigma^{-1} u \| + \|\nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \\

&\leq  \| [\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) - c]\sigma^{-1} u \| + \|\mathbb{E}[\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}} (x + \sigma u, y) \sigma^{-1} u]\| \\

&\leq  \| 2b \sigma^{-1} u \| + 2b\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{d},

\end{equs}
since $|\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}}^{\hat{x}}| \leq b$ and $|c|\leq b$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the deviation by norms of u.

nodes.name: Gaussian concentration
nodes.statement:
Therefore, since $u \sim N(0,I_d)$ is a gaussian random vector, Inequality \eqref{eq:e4} implies that

\begin{align} \mathbb{P}(\|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \geq t)

&\leq \mathbb{P}\left(\| 2b \sigma^{-1} u \| + 2b\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{d} \geq t\right)\\

 &\leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{8\left(\frac{2b\sqrt{d}}{\sigma}\right)^2}\right)  \qquad \forall t \geq 0,
\end{align}

where the last inequality holds by a standard concentration inequality for Gaussians \cite{hanson1971bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Gaussian concentration (Hanson-Wright).

nodes.name: Tail bound for the stochastic gradient
nodes.statement:
\mathbb{P}(\|\hat{\Gamma}^{\hat{x}}_{\varepsilon^{\circ}} (x,y) - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon^\circ, \sigma}^{\hat{x}}(x,y)\| \geq t)

&\leq \mathbb{P}\left(\| 2b \sigma^{-1} u \| + 2b\sigma^{-1}\sqrt{d} \geq t\right)\\

 &\leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{8\left(\frac{2b\sqrt{d}}{\sigma}\right)^2}\right)  \qquad \forall t \geq 0,
nodes.label: eq:e5

nodes.name: Low-magnitude stochastic gradient
conclusions: \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathcal{H}^{x^\star}_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}}(x^\star, y^\star)\right\| \, \bigg | \, (x^\star, y^\star) \right] \leq 10 b \gamma_1 \sqrt{d}\sigma^{-1} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1}.
nodes.statement_short: With probability 1-omega the stochastic gradient H at the output has expected norm O(b gamma1 sqrt(d)/sigma log(1/gamma1)).
nodes.label: prop_SGVariance

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.8
nodes.statement_short: A large expected stochastic gradient forces a gamma1-decrease with probability >= 2gamma1 per random trial; the I3 hill-climbing trials make missing it unlikely, union-bounded over iterations.

nodes.name: Suppose large stochastic gradient
nodes.statement_short: Assume the expected stochastic gradient is large at iteration i.

nodes.name: Gaussian tail split
nodes.statement:
Then, 
\begin{equs}
  {}& 10 b \gamma_1 \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\sigma} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1} < \mathbb{E}\left[\|\mathcal{H}_{\varepsilon_{i}}^{x_{i}}(x_{i}, y_{i})\| \big | (x_{i}, y_{i}) \right] \\
 
 &= \mathbb{E}[  \| \zeta \sigma^{-1}(\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}}^{x_{i}}(x_{i}  + \sigma \zeta,y_{i}) - \mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}}^{x_{i}}(x_{i} ,y_{i}))  \| \, \, \big | \,\, (x_{i}, y_{i}) ] \\
 
 &= \mathbb{E}\left[ \| \zeta \sigma^{-1}(\min(h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i}  + \sigma \zeta,y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_{i}} (x_{i}, y_{i})) - \min(h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i} ,y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i} ,y_{i})))  \|  \, \, \big | \, \,  (x_{i}, y_{i}) \right]\\

  &= \mathbb{E}\left[ \| \zeta \sigma^{-1} (\min(h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i}  + \sigma \zeta,y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_{i}} (x_{i}, y_{i})) - h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i} ,y_{i}))  \| \,  \big | \,  (x_{i}, y_{i}) \right]\\
  
    &= \mathbb{E}\left[ \left\| \zeta \sigma^{-1}  \right\| \times |\min(h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i}  + \sigma \zeta,y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_{i}} (x_{i}, y_{i})) - h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i} ,y_{i})) | \, \, \,  \big | \, \, \, (x_{i}, y_{i}) \right]\\

     &\leq \mathbb{E}\left[  \sqrt{d} \sigma^{-1} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1}\times | \min(h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i}  + \sigma \zeta,y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_{i}} (x_{i}, y_{i})) - h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i} ,y_{i})| \, \, \,  \big | \,  \, \, (x_{i}, y_{i}) \right]\\
     
     &\qquad \qquad \qquad +\mathbb{P}\left(\|\zeta\| \geq  \sqrt{d} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1} \right) \times \mathbb{E}\left[ \| \zeta \sigma^{-1} \| \times 2b  \, \, \,  \big | \, \,  \,  \|\zeta\| \geq  \sqrt{d} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1} \right]\\
     
     &\leq \mathbb{E}\left[  \sqrt{d} \sigma^{-1} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1}\times |\min(h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i}  + \sigma \zeta,y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_{i}} (x_{i}, y_{i})) - h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i} ,y_{i})| \, \, \, \big | \, \, \, (x_{i}, y_{i}) \right]\\

        &\qquad \qquad \qquad + 2 \frac{\gamma_1}{2} \times \mathbb{E}\left[ \| \zeta \sigma^{-1} \| b  \, \, \, \big | \, \, \,  \|\zeta\| \geq  \sqrt{d} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1} \right]\\
  
     &\leq \sqrt{d} \sigma^{-1} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1} \mathbb{E}[ | (\min(h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i}  + \sigma \zeta,y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_{i}} (x_{i}, y_{i})) - h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i} ,y_{i})) |  \, \, \, \big | \, \, \, (x_{i}, y_{i}) ] + 2b \gamma_1 \sigma^{-1} \sqrt{d} \log\frac{2}{\gamma_1}.

 \end{equs}
 
 where the last two inequalities hold by a standard concentration bound for Gaussians \cite{hanson1971bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Split on the Gaussian tail to bound the expectation.

nodes.name: Decrease has probability >= 2 gamma1
nodes.statement_short: Hence a gamma1-sized change occurs with probability at least 2gamma1.

nodes.name: Bad events E_i
nodes.statement:
For any $i \in [i_{\mathrm{max}} ]$, let  $E_{i}$ be the ``bad" event that we have both 
\begin{equs} \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{H}_{\varepsilon_{i}}^{x_{i}} (x_{i}, y_{i})\| \, \, \, \big | \, \, \, (x_i, y_i)] > 10 b \gamma_1 \sqrt{d} \sigma^{-1} \log\frac{2b}{\gamma_1},
\end{equs}

and

\begin{equs} \left| \min(h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i} + \sigma \zeta_{i j}, y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i}, y_{i}) ) - h_{\varepsilon_{i}}(x_{i}, y_{i}) \right| \leq 2\gamma_1,
\end{equs}

for every $j \in [\mathcal{I}_3]$.
nodes.statement_short: Define bad events E_i.

nodes.name: Union bound
nodes.statement_short: Each E_i has probability <= omega/i_max; union bound gives omega.

nodes.name: Stopping check at output
nodes.statement:
Now, whenever the Algorithm outputs a point $(x_{i^\star}, y_{i^\star}) = (x^\star, y^\star)$, it first checks that the inequality in Line \ref{HillClimbing} does not hold for the point $(x^\star + \sigma \zeta_{i^\star j},y^\star)$ for the random vector $\zeta_{i^\star j} \sim N(0,I_d)$, and it repeats this check $\mathcal{I}_3$ times before stopping.  In other words, we have that
\begin{equs} f(x^\star + \sigma \zeta_{i^\star j}, \mathcal{Y}_{j}) > f(x^\star, y^\star) - \gamma_1 \qquad \forall j \in [\mathcal{I}_3],
\end{equs}
for a sequence of independent random vectors $\zeta_{i^\star 1}, \ldots, \zeta_{i^\star \mathcal{I}_3} \sim N(0,I_d)$.  Here we denote by $\mathcal{Y}_{j}$ the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:InnerMaxLoop} for inputs  $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow x^\star + \sigma \zeta_{i^\star j}$,  $\mathsf{y}^0 \leftarrow y^\star$, and $\varepsilon' \leftarrow \varepsilon_{i^\star}(1+\delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: At termination all I3 hill-climbing trials failed.

nodes.name: Translate to h
nodes.statement_short: Use the definition of h and Proposition 7.6.

nodes.name: Truncated decrease small
nodes.statement_short: The truncated decrease is below gamma1 for every trial.

nodes.name: Small truncated decrease at the output
nodes.statement: \left| \min(h_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}}(x^\star + \sigma \zeta_{i^\star j}, y^\star), h_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}}(x^\star, y^\star) ) - h_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}}(x^\star, y^\star) \right| <  \gamma_1.
nodes.label: eq:f5

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Outside the bad events the stochastic gradient is small.

nodes.name: First-order stationary condition
nodes.statement:
\begin{equs} \mathbb{P}\left(\left\| \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}, \sigma}^{x^\star}(x^\star,y^\star)\right\| > 10 b \gamma_1 \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\sigma} \log\frac{2b}{\gamma_1} \right) \leq \omega.
\end{equs}
nodes.section: 7.5.3 Showing $x^\star$ is an approximate local minimum of $h_\varepsilon(\cdot, y^\star)$
conclusions: \mathbb{P}\left(\left\| \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}, \sigma}^{x^\star}(x^\star,y^\star)\right\| > 10 b \gamma_1 \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\sigma} \log\frac{2b}{\gamma_1} \right) \leq \omega.
nodes.label: Prop_first_order_x

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.9
nodes.section: 7.5.3 Showing $x^\star$ is an approximate local minimum of $h_\varepsilon(\cdot, y^\star)$
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality with the unbiasedness of Proposition 7.7 and the bound of Proposition 7.8.

nodes.name: Gradient bound for smoothed h at the output
nodes.statement: \| \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}, \sigma}^{x^\star}(x^\star,y^\star)\| \leq 10 b \gamma_1 \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\sigma} \log\frac{2b}{\gamma_1}.
nodes.section: 7.5.3 Showing $x^\star$ is an approximate local minimum of $h_\varepsilon(\cdot, y^\star)$
nodes.label: eq:g12

nodes.name: Second-order stationary condition
nodes.section: 7.5.3 Showing $x^\star$ is an approximate local minimum of $h_\varepsilon(\cdot, y^\star)$
conclusions: \lambda_{\mathrm{min}}\left(\nabla^2_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}, \sigma}^{x^\star}(x^\star, y^\star) \right) \geq - \frac{1}{5}\sqrt{\varepsilon_{i^\star}}.
nodes.label: Prop_NoisySGD

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.10
nodes.statement:
In this proof, it will be convenient to write $X_{k}$ which appears inside the For loop (Lines \ref{RebootStart}-\ref{RebootEnd} in Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max}) with an index $j$ indicating the value that $X_{k}$ takes during the $j$th For loop.  Specifically, instead of $X_{k}$, we will write $X^{j}_{k}$.  In a simmilar manner, we right $u_{i k}$ in place of $u$.



From Line \ref{PSGD_start} of Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max} we have that
\begin{equs} h^{k} = \min(f(X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, \mathcal{Y}), f(x_{i}, y_{i})),
\end{equs}
where $\mathcal{Y} \leftarrow \mathsf{y}_{\mathrm{LocalMax}}$ is the output $\mathsf{y}_{\mathrm{LocalMax}}$ of Algorithm \ref{alg:InnerMaxLoop} with inputs $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}$,  $\mathsf{y}^0 \leftarrow y_{i}$, $\varepsilon' \leftarrow \varepsilon_{i}(1+\delta)$.

Therefore, by the definition of the function $h$ (Equation \eqref{eq:z1}), we have that

\begin{equs} f(X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, \mathcal{Y}) = h_{\varepsilon_i} (X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, y_{i}).
\end{equs}



\noindent
Moreover, by Proposition \ref{Prop_fixed_point}, we have that
\begin{equs} f(x_{i}, y_{i}) = h_{\varepsilon_i}(x_{i}, y_{i}).
\end{equs}


\noindent
  Therefore, Equations \eqref{eq:g15},  \eqref{eq:g16} and \eqref{eq:g17}, together imply that

\begin{equs} h^{k} &= \min(f(X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, \mathcal{Y}),  \, \, f(x_{i}, y_{i}))\\
 & =  \min(h_{\varepsilon_i} (X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, y_{i}),  \, \, h_{\varepsilon_i}(x_{i}, y_{i})).
\end{equs}


\noindent
In Line \ref{PSGD_end} of Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max} we have that  $\Gamma_{k} = (h^{k} - h^{k-1}) \frac{1}{\sigma} u_{i k}$.  Therefore, Equation \eqref{eq:g2} implies that
\begin{equs} \Gamma_{k} &= (h^{k} - h^{k-1}) \frac{1}{\sigma} u_{i k}\\

&= [\min(h_{\varepsilon_i} (X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_i}(x_{i}, y_{i})) - h_{k-1}]\frac{1}{\sigma} u _{i k}\\

& = [\min(\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon_i}^{x_{i}} (X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, y_{i})) - h_{k-1}]\frac{1}{\sigma} u _{i k}.
\end{equs}


\noindent Therefore by Equation \eqref{eq:g3} and Proposition \ref{lemma_SG}, and since $h_{k-1}$ is independent of $\sigma u_{i k}$, we have that

\begin{equs} \mathbb{E}[\Gamma_{k}]= \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(X^{j}_{k-1},y_{i}),
\end{equs}
and
\begin{equation} \mathbb{P}(\|\Gamma_{k} - \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(X^{j}_{k-1},y_{i})\| \geq t) \leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{8\left(\frac{2b\sqrt{d}}{\sigma}\right)^2}\right)  \qquad \forall t \geq 0.
\end{equation}

In other words, $\Gamma_{k}$ is a stochastic gradient for $\mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(X^{j}_{k-1},y_{i})$ (Equation \eqref{eq:g4}) which satisfies a concentration property (Inequality \eqref{eq:g5}).



Since $\Gamma_{k}$ is a stochastic gradient  with concentration properties for a smooth function, we can apply results from \cite{NonconvexOptimizationForML} which, roughly speaking, say that stochastic gradient descent with added Gaussian noise can escape saddle points in polynomial time.

More specifically, Lemma 25 of \cite{NonconvexOptimizationForML}, together with Equations \eqref{eq:g4} and \eqref{eq:g5}, imply that if at any iteration $i$ of the For loop in Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max} (Lines \ref{RebootStart}-\ref{RebootEnd}) we have

\begin{equs} \|\nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(x_{i},y_{i})\| \leq  \varepsilon_{i}/50,
\end{equs}

and
\begin{equs} \lambda_{\min}(\nabla_{{x}}^2 \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(x_{i},y_{i})) \leq -   \sqrt{\varepsilon_{i}}/10,
\end{equs}

then 

\begin{equs} \mathbb{P}(\mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}( X^{j}_{\mathcal{I}_2}, y_{i}) - \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(x_{i}, y_{i}) \leq -\gamma_1) \geq \frac{1}{6},
\end{equs}

as long as the hyper-parameters $\gamma_1, \mathcal{I}_2, \eta, \alpha$ satisfy 
$$\gamma_1 \leq \varepsilon^{\nicefrac{3}{2}} \sigma^{15.5} (b^{2.5} \mathsf{c} \log^5( bd\sqrt{\sigma \varepsilon}))^{-1},$$ 

$$\mathcal{I}_2 \geq \mathsf{c} \eta^{-1} \varepsilon^{-\nicefrac{1}{2}} \log(bd\sqrt{\sigma \varepsilon}) ,$$ 
$$\eta \leq \frac{\sigma^9}{b^4 d^2} (b^2 (1+ 10 b d \sigma^{-12} \varepsilon^{-2}) \mathsf{c} \log^9( bd\sqrt{\sigma \varepsilon}))^{-1},$$  
$$\alpha = \eta \mathsf{c}\log( bd\sqrt{\sigma \varepsilon}) \sqrt{1+ b^2 d^2 \sigma^{-2}},$$

  where $\mathsf{c}$ is a universal constant.



For every $i \in [i_{\max}]$, let $\mathcal{E}_i$ be the ``bad" event that we have that both of the following Equations \eqref{eq:g8} and \eqref{eq:g9} hold:

\begin{equation} \|\nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(x_{i},y_{i})\| \leq \frac{1}{50}\varepsilon_{i}, \qquad  \lambda_{\min}(\nabla_{{x}}^2 \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(x_{i},y_{i})) \leq - \frac{1}{10} \sqrt{\varepsilon_{i}}
\end{equation}

and

\begin{equs} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}( X^{j}_{\mathcal{I}_2}, y_{i}) - \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i}, \sigma}^{x_{i}}(x_{i}, y_{i}) > -\gamma_1 \qquad \forall j\in \mathcal{I}_4.
\end{equs}

\noindent Then Inequality \eqref{eq:g14} implies that
\begin{equs} \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_i) \leq \left(1-\frac{1}{6}\right)^{\mathcal{I}_4} \leq \frac{\omega}{i_{\max}},
\end{equs}
since $\mathcal{I}_4 \geq 6\log(\frac{i_{\max}}{\omega})$, where $i_{\max} = O(\frac{b}{\gamma_1})$ is an upper bound given in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemma:RunningTime} on the number of iterations of the While loop in Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max}.

 \noindent
Therefore,
\begin{equation} {\textstyle \mathbb{P}(\bigcup_{i=1}^{i_{\max}} \mathcal{E}_{i}) \leq \sum_{i=1}^{{i}_{\max}}  \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{i}) \stackrel{\textrm{Eq.} \ref{eq:f10}}{\leq} {i}_{\max} \times \frac{\omega}{{i}_{\max}}  = \omega.}
\end{equation}


\noindent Now, since we set $\gamma_1 \leq \frac{\varepsilon \sigma}{10^3 b \sqrt{d} \log(\frac{2b}{\gamma_1}) }$,  Proposition \ref{Prop_first_order_x} Implies that 
\begin{equs} \mathbb{P}\left(\| \nabla_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}, \sigma}^{x^\star}(x^\star,y^\star)\| > \frac{1}{100}\varepsilon\right) \leq \omega.
\end{equs}



\noindent
Now, the condition in Line \ref{SuccessStart} of Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max} implies that Inequality \eqref{eq:g9}  holds for all $j\in \mathcal{I}_4$ when the value of $i$ is $i^\star$.  Therefore, Inequalities \eqref{eq:g13}, and \eqref{eq:g11}, together with the definition of $\mathcal{E}_i$ (\eqref{eq:g8} and \eqref{eq:g9}) imply that
\begin{equs} \lambda_{\mathrm{min}}(\nabla^2_{{x}} \mathfrak{h}_{\varepsilon_{i^\star}, \sigma}^{x^\star}(x^\star, y^\star)) \geq - \frac{1}{10}\sqrt{\varepsilon_{i^\star}},
 \end{equs}
 with probability at least $1-2\omega$.

nodes.name: h^k in terms of h
nodes.statement:
From Line \ref{PSGD_start} of Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max} we have that
\begin{equs} h^{k} = \min(f(X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, \mathcal{Y}), f(x_{i}, y_{i})),
\end{equs}
where $\mathcal{Y} \leftarrow \mathsf{y}_{\mathrm{LocalMax}}$ is the output $\mathsf{y}_{\mathrm{LocalMax}}$ of Algorithm \ref{alg:InnerMaxLoop} with inputs $\mathsf{x} \leftarrow X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}$,  $\mathsf{y}^0 \leftarrow y_{i}$, $\varepsilon' \leftarrow \varepsilon_{i}(1+\delta)$.

Therefore, by the definition of the function $h$ (Equation \eqref{eq:z1}), we have that

\begin{equs} f(X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, \mathcal{Y}) = h_{\varepsilon_i} (X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, y_{i}).
\end{equs}



\noindent
Moreover, by Proposition \ref{Prop_fixed_point}, we have that
\begin{equs} f(x_{i}, y_{i}) = h_{\varepsilon_i}(x_{i}, y_{i}).
\end{equs}

 & =  \min(h_{\varepsilon_i} (X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, y_{i}),  \, \, h_{\varepsilon_i}(x_{i}, y_{i})).
\end{equs}


\noindent
In Line \ref{PSGD_end} of Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max} we have that  $\Gamma_{k} = (h^{k} - h^{k-1}) \frac{1}{\sigma} u_{i k}$.  Therefore, Equation \eqref{eq:g2} implies that
\begin{equs} \Gamma_{k} &= (h^{k} - h^{k-1}) \frac{1}{\sigma} u_{i k}\\

&= [\min(h_{\varepsilon_i} (X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, y_{i}), h_{\varepsilon_i}(x_{i}, y_{i})) - h_{k-1}]\frac{1}{\sigma} u _{i k}\\

& = [\min(\mathbbm{h}_{\varepsilon_i}^{x_{i}} (X^{j}_{k-1} + \sigma u_{i k}, y_{i})) - h_{k-1}]\frac{1}{\sigma} u _{i k}.
\end{equs}

nodes.name: Convergence and oracle calls
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Showing convergence, and bounding the number of oracle calls.}

By Lemma \ref{lemma:RunningTime}, we have that Algorithm \ref{alg:LocalMin-max} terminates and outputs a point $(x^\star, y^\star) \in \mathbb{R}^d$ after  $$O\left(\frac{b}{\gamma_1} \times (\mathcal{I}_2 \mathcal{I}_4 + \mathcal{I}_3) \times \frac{b}{ \mu_1 \mu_3^2 L_{}}\right) = \mathrm{poly}\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}, d, b, L_{}, \frac{1}{\sigma}\right)$$ gradient, function, and Hessian evaluations.  In particular, if $b, L \geq 1$ and if $\sigma, \varepsilon \leq 1$, the number of gradient, function, and Hessian evaluations can be simplified to $O\left(\frac{d^{8} L^2 b^{37}}{\varepsilon^{19}\sigma^{132}}\right)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.1 gives a polynomial number of oracle calls.

nodes.name: Greedy adversarial equilibrium
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Showing that $(x^\star, y^\star)$ is greedy adversarial equilibrium for $f$.}

 Inequalities \eqref{eq:h5} and \eqref{eq:h6} together imply that, with probability at least $1-4 \omega$, the point $(x^\star, y^\star)$ is an $(\varepsilon^\star, \sigma)$-greedy adversarial equilibrium, where $\varepsilon^\star = \varepsilon_{i^\star} \leq \varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Both conditions of Definition 2.5 hold.

nodes.name: Greedy adversarial equilibria have small duality gap under strong convexity-concavity
nodes.section: A Greedy adversarial equilibrium in the strongly convex-strongly concave setting
also_stated_at: If $f$ is $1$-strongly convex- strongly concave, then for  $\varepsilon>0$ and small enough $\sigma$, we show that at any $(\varepsilon, \sigma)$-greedy adversarial equilibrium $(x^\star, y^\star)$ the duality gap satisfies $$\max_{y \in \mathbb{R}^d} f(x^\star, y)-\min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} f(x, y^\star) \leq O(\varepsilon^2);$$ see Theorem \ref{Thm_strongly_convex_concave} in Appendix \ref{sec:convex_concave} for a precise statement of this result and its proof.
assumptions: for some $\alpha, L >0$ the function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is $C^2$-smooth, $\alpha$-strongly convex in $x$, $\alpha$-strongly concave in $y$, and has $L$-Lipschitz gradients and $L$-Lipschitz Hessian

$(x^\star, y^\star)$ is an $(\varepsilon, \sigma)$-greedy adversarial equilibrium, for any $\varepsilon>0$ and any $0< \sigma \leq \frac{\varepsilon^3 \alpha}{10d^{\nicefrac{3}{2}} L^3 (\alpha+1) \log(L\frac{\alpha+1}{\alpha})}.$
conclusions: \max_{z \in \mathbb{R}^d} f(x^\star, z) - \min_{w\in \mathbb{R}^d} f(w, y^\star) \leq 26\frac{\varepsilon^2}{\alpha}.
nodes.statement_short: For alpha-strongly convex-concave f, any (eps, sigma)-greedy adversarial equilibrium with small sigma has duality gap at most 26 eps^2/alpha.
nodes.label: Thm_strongly_convex_concave

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem A.1
nodes.statement:
Since $(x^\star, y^\star)$ is an $(\varepsilon, \sigma)$-greedy adversarial equilibrium, $\|\nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star)\| \leq \varepsilon$.

Therefore, since $f(x,y)$ is $\alpha$-strongly concave in $y$, we have that
\begin{equs} \|y^\star - \mathrm{argmax}_z f(x^\star, z)\| \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}.
\end{equs}

\noindent
Recall the notation
   
   \begin{equs}
   S(x) :=  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)}\left [\min(g_\varepsilon(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  g_\varepsilon(x^\star, y^\star)) \right].
   \end{equs}
   
   from Definition \ref{def:local_min-max_formal}.
   
   From the proof of Proposition \ref{Prop_fixed_point} we have that $f(x^\star, y^\star) = g_\varepsilon(x^\star, y^\star)$.  Thus,
   
\begin{equs}
      S(x) =  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[\min(g_\varepsilon(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star), f(x^\star, y^\star)) \right].
\end{equs}
   
   \noindent
   Let 
   \begin{equs}
   \hat{S}(x) = \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)}\left [\min(g_\varepsilon(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star)) - \min(f(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star))  \right].
   \end{equs}
    \noindent
   Then, by the formula in Equation \eqref{eq_stochastic_gradient_formula}, we have
   
\begin{equs} \|\nabla_x \hat{S}(x)\| &=  \left \|\mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left [ \frac{\zeta}{\sigma}\left [\min(g_\varepsilon(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star)) - \min(f(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star))  \right] \right]\right \|\\

& \leq  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left [ \frac{\|\zeta\|}{\sigma} \times \left \| \min(g_\varepsilon(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star)) - \min(f(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star))  \right\| \right].
\end{equs}


 \noindent
Suppose now that $\zeta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and let $\varphi$ be any $\varepsilon$-greedy path starting at the point $y^\star$ which seeks to maximize $f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, \cdot)$.



Thus, since $f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, \cdot)$ increases at rate at least $\varepsilon$ along the greedy path, and $f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, \cdot)$ is $\alpha$-strongly concave, we must have that the greedy path reaches a point $p$ where
$$\|\nabla_y f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, p)\| \leq \varepsilon,$$

after the path has traveled a distance of at most $\|p-y^\star\| \leq (\|\nabla_y f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star)\|-\varepsilon) \times \frac{1}{\alpha}$.  

Thus, since the value of $f$ must continuously increase along the greedy path, and $f(x,y)$ is strongly concave in $y$, we have that
\begin{equs} {}&\left | \min(g_\varepsilon(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star)) - \min(f(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star))  \right |\\

&\leq \left | g_\varepsilon(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star) - f(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star)  \right |\\ 

&\leq (\|\nabla_y f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star)\|-\varepsilon) \times \frac{1}{\alpha} \times \|\nabla_y f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star)\|,
\end{equs}
\noindent
Therefore, combining Inequalities \eqref{eq_z1} and \eqref{eq_z2}, we get
\begin{equs}
{}&\|\nabla_x \hat{S}(x)\| 
 \stackrel{\textrm{Eq.}\ref{eq_z1}, \ref{eq_z2}}{\leq} \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left [ \frac{\|\zeta\|}{\sigma} \times (\|\nabla_y f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star)\|-\varepsilon) \times \frac{1}{\alpha} \times \|\nabla_y f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star)\| \right]\\
&\leq\mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \bigg [ \frac{20\sqrt{d} \log\left(d\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}\right)}{\sigma} \times (\|\nabla_y f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star)\|-\varepsilon) \times \frac{1}{\alpha}\\
&\qquad \qquad \qquad  \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad  \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \times \left(\varepsilon + L \sigma 20\sqrt{d} \log\left(d\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}\right)\right)\bigg]\\

&+ \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left [ \frac{\|\zeta\|}{\sigma} \times (L\sigma\|\zeta\|) \times \frac{1}{\alpha} \times(\varepsilon + L\sigma\|\zeta\|) \times \mathbbm{1}\bigg\{\|\zeta\| \geq 20\sqrt{d} \log\left(d\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}\right) \bigg\} \right ]\\

&
 \stackrel{\textrm{Lemma }\ref{lemma_strong}}{\leq} \frac{20\sqrt{d} \log(d(\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon})}{\sigma} \times \left( \frac{1}{2 \varepsilon}L^2  \sigma^2 d  +   \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d \right ) \times \frac{1}{\alpha}\times \left(\varepsilon + L \sigma 20\sqrt{d} \log\left(d\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}\right)\right)\\

&+ \frac{L^2 \sigma + \varepsilon}{\alpha}\mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left [ \|\zeta\|^3 \times \mathbbm{1}\bigg\{\|\zeta\| \geq 20\sqrt{d} \log\left(d\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}\right)\bigg\} \right ]\\

& \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2} + \frac{L^2 \sigma + \varepsilon}{\alpha}\mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left [ \|\zeta\|^4 \times \mathbbm{1}\bigg\{\|\zeta\| \geq 20\sqrt{d} \log\left(d\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}\right)\bigg\} \right ]\\

& \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2} + \int_{(20\sqrt{d} \log(d(\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}))^4 }^{\infty} \mathbb{P}(\|\zeta\|^4 \geq t) \mathrm{d}t\\

 & = \frac{\varepsilon}{2} + \int_{(20\sqrt{d} \log(d(\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}))^4 }^{\infty} \mathbb{P}(|\zeta\| \geq t^{\nicefrac{1}{4}}) \mathrm{d}t\\
 
  & \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2} + \int_{(20\sqrt{d} \log(d(\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}))^4 }^{\infty} e^{-\frac{\sqrt{t} - d}{8}} \mathrm{d}t\\
  
    & \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2} + e^{\frac{d}{8}} \left( -16(\sqrt{t}+8) e^{-\frac{\sqrt{t}}{8}} \right) \bigg|_{20\sqrt{d} \log\left(d\frac{L(\alpha+1)}{\alpha \varepsilon}\right)^4 }^{\infty} \\
   & \leq \varepsilon,
\end{equs}
where the third inequality is by  Lemma \ref{lemma_strong}, the fourth inequality holds since  since $\sigma \leq \frac{\varepsilon^3 \alpha}{10 d^{\nicefrac{3}{2}} L^3 (\alpha+1) \log(L\frac{\alpha+1}{\alpha \varepsilon})}$, and the sixth inequality is a standard concentration bound for Gaussians \cite{hanson1971bound}.


Define $R(x) :=  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)}\left [\min(f(x  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star),  f(x^\star, y^\star)) \right]$ for all $x\in \mathbb{R}^d$.

Since $(x^\star, y^\star)$ is an $(\varepsilon, \sigma)$-greedy adversarial point, we have $\|\nabla_x S(x)\| \leq \varepsilon$.


Then
\begin{equs} \| \nabla_x R(x^\star) \| = \| \nabla_x S(x) - \nabla_x \hat{S}(x) \| \leq  \| \nabla_x S(x)\| +  \| \nabla_x \hat{S}(x) \| &\stackrel{\textrm{Eq.}\ref{eq_z3}}{\leq} 2\varepsilon.
\end{equs}
 \noindent
  Since $f(\cdot, y^\star)$ is convex,
\begin{equs} \mathbb{P}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)}(\min(f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star) \geq  f(x^\star, y^\star)) \geq \frac{1}{2}.
\end{equs}
 
 Thus, since $f$ is also $L$-Lipschitz,
\begin{equs}
\| \nabla_x R(x^\star) \| \stackrel{\textrm{Eq.}\eqref{eq_strong_2}}{\geq}\frac{1}{2}\|\nabla_x f(x^\star, y^\star)\| - \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)}[L\sigma \|\zeta\|] =  \frac{1}{2}\|\nabla_x f(x^\star, y^\star)\| - L \sigma \sqrt{d}.
\end{equs}
 \noindent
Thus,
\begin{equs} \|\nabla_x f(x^\star, y^\star)\| &\leq  2\| \nabla_x R(x^\star) \|  + 2L \sigma \sqrt{d}\\

& \stackrel{\textrm{Eq.}\eqref{eq_z4}}{\leq} 4\varepsilon +  2L \sigma \sqrt{d} \\

&\leq 5\varepsilon,
\end{equs}

since $\sigma \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2Ld}$.

\noindent
Since $f$ is $\alpha$-strongly convex, Inequality \eqref{eq_strong_1} implies that

\begin{equs} \|x^\star - \operatornamewithlimits{argmin}_w f(w, y^\star)\| \leq 5\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}.
\end{equs}

\noindent
Now, since $f(\cdot, y^\star)$ is $\alpha$-strongly convex, Inequality \eqref{eq_strong_x} implies that
\begin{equs} f(x^\star, y^\star) - \min_{w\in \mathbb{R}^d} f(w, y^\star) \leq  25\frac{\varepsilon^2}{\alpha}.
\end{equs}

And since $f(x^\star, \cdot)$ is  $\alpha$-strongly concave, 

Inequality \eqref{eq_strong_y} implies that
\begin{equs} \max_{z\in \mathbb{R^d}} f(x^\star, z) - f(x^\star, y^\star) \leq \frac{\varepsilon^2}{\alpha}.
\end{equs}

\noindent
Combining Inequalities \eqref{eq_z5} and \eqref{eq_z6}, we get

\begin{equs} \max_{z \in \mathbb{R}^d} f(x^\star, z) - \min_{w\in \mathbb{R}^d} f(w, y^\star) \leq 26\frac{\varepsilon^2}{\alpha}.
\end{equs}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.2
nodes.statement:
Since $f$ is $C^2$-smooth, we have that




\begin{equs} \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} &[ \|\nabla_y f(x^\star  + \sigma \zeta, y^\star)\|]\\
 &= \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left \| \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) + \int_{0}^{\sigma\|\zeta\|}  \nabla_{xy}^2   f(x^\star  + t \frac{\zeta}{\|\zeta\|}, y^\star)  \frac{\zeta}{\|\zeta\|}  \mathrm{d}t \right \| \right ]\\

&\leq \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[  \int_{0}^{\sigma\|\zeta\|} \left \| \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star)+   \nabla_{xy}^2   f(x^\star  + t \frac{\zeta}{\|\zeta\|}, y^\star) \frac{\zeta}{\|\zeta\|}  \right \|\mathrm{d}t \right ]\\

&\leq  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[  \int_{0}^{\sigma\|\zeta\|} \left \| \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) + \nabla_{xy}^2   f(x^\star, y^\star) \frac{\zeta}{\|\zeta\|}  \right \| \mathrm{d}t  \right ]\\
& \qquad \qquad+   \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \int_{0}^{\sigma\|\zeta\|}   \left \| [\nabla_{xy}^2   f(x^\star  + t \frac{\zeta}{\|\zeta\|}, y^\star)  - \nabla_{xy}^2   f(x^\star, y^\star)] \frac{\zeta}{\|\zeta\|}  \right \|\mathrm{d}t \right ]\\

&\leq   \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left \| \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) + \nabla_{xy}^2   f(x^\star, y^\star) \sigma \zeta  \right \|   \right ] + \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \int_{0}^{\sigma\|\zeta\|}   L \sigma \|\zeta\| \mathrm{d}t \right ]\\

&\leq  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left \| \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) + L  \sigma \zeta  \right \|   \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \|\zeta\|^2   \right ]\\

&=  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left \langle \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) + L  \sigma \zeta, \, \, \, \, \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) + L  \sigma \zeta   \right \rangle^{\nicefrac{1}{2}}   \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d\\

&=  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left( \|\nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star)\|^2+ 2 \left \langle \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) , \, \, L  \sigma \zeta  \right \rangle, \, \, \, \,+ L^2  \sigma^2 \|\zeta\|^2  \right )^{\nicefrac{1}{2}} \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d\\

&\leq \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left( \|\nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star)\|^2 + L^2  \sigma^2 \|\zeta\|^2  \right )^{\nicefrac{1}{2}} \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d\\

&\leq \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left( \varepsilon^2 + L^2  \sigma^2 \|\zeta\|^2  \right )^{\nicefrac{1}{2}} \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d\\

&\leq  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[  \varepsilon + \frac{1}{2 \varepsilon}L^2  \sigma^2 \|\zeta\|^2 \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d\\

&= \varepsilon + \frac{1}{2 \varepsilon}L^2  \sigma^2 d  +   \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d,
\end{equs}
where the third inequality is due to the fact that $f$ has $L$-Lipschitz Hessian.  The fourth ineqaulity holds because $-L I_{2d} \preceq \nabla^2   f(x^\star, y^\star) \preceq L I_{2d}$ because $f$ has $L$-Lipschitz gradient, $\nabla^2   f(x^\star, y^\star)$ is symmetric (and therefore is diagonalizable by an orthogonal matrix) and $\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)$.

The fifth inequality holds since $\sqrt{\cdot}$ is concave, and the distribution of $\langle \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) , \, L  \sigma \zeta \rangle$ is symmetric about $0$.

And the seventh inequality is due to the fact that the linear approximation to the function $\sqrt{t}$ at $t=\varepsilon^2$ gives an upper bound for the function $\sqrt{t}$ for all $t \geq \varepsilon^2$, since the function $\sqrt{t}$ is concave.

&\leq \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left( \|\nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star)\|^2 + L^2  \sigma^2 \|\zeta\|^2  \right )^{\nicefrac{1}{2}} \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d\\

&\leq \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[ \left( \varepsilon^2 + L^2  \sigma^2 \|\zeta\|^2  \right )^{\nicefrac{1}{2}} \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d\\

&\leq  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)} \left[  \varepsilon + \frac{1}{2 \varepsilon}L^2  \sigma^2 \|\zeta\|^2 \right ]  + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d\\

&= \varepsilon + \frac{1}{2 \varepsilon}L^2  \sigma^2 d  +   \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 L d,

where the third inequality is due to the fact that $f$ has $L$-Lipschitz Hessian.

nodes.statement:
The fourth ineqaulity holds because $-L I_{2d} \preceq \nabla^2   f(x^\star, y^\star) \preceq L I_{2d}$ because $f$ has $L$-Lipschitz gradient, $\nabla^2   f(x^\star, y^\star)$ is symmetric (and therefore is diagonalizable by an orthogonal matrix) and $\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)$.

The fifth inequality holds since $\sqrt{\cdot}$ is concave, and the distribution of $\langle \nabla_y f(x^\star, y^\star) , \, L  \sigma \zeta \rangle$ is symmetric about $0$.

And the seventh inequality is due to the fact that the linear approximation to the function $\sqrt{t}$ at $t=\varepsilon^2$ gives an upper bound for the function $\sqrt{t}$ for all $t \geq \varepsilon^2$, since the function $\sqrt{t}$ is concave.
nodes.statement_short: Justify the fourth, fifth and seventh inequalities.

nodes.name: Properties of the bump function
nodes.statement: In particular, we note that $\psi$ is $1$-lipschitz with $8$-Lipschitz gradient, and that $\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}\psi(x) =\frac{1}{e}$ and $\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}\psi(x) = 0$.  We also note that $\psi$ is $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ with all its derivatives vanishing outside of the ball $B(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Hardness of nonconvex optimization for deterministic algorithms
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}(g)$ be any deterministic algorithm which takes as input any function $g: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$,  and has output $\tilde{x}(g) \in \mathbb{R}^d$ \footnote{We only allow one output point, since then the algorithm could just output all the points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without making any oracle calls.}, where $\mathcal{A}(g)$ can only access the function $g$ by zeroth- first- and second- order oracle access to $g$. 

 Then there exists an objective function $\mathfrak{f}: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ that is 1-Lipschitz, with 8-Lipschitz gradient, and for which $\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d} \mathfrak{f}(x) - \inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d} \mathfrak{f}(x) \leq \frac{1}{e}$, with global minimizer $x^\star \in B(0,10)$, such that the algorithm $\mathcal{A}(\mathfrak{f})$ must make at least $2^d$ oracle calls to find an $\varepsilon$-global minimizer $x^\circ$ of $\mathfrak{f}$ with $\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2e}$ for which $\mathfrak{f}(x^\circ) - \mathfrak{f}(x^\star) \leq \varepsilon$.
nodes.section: B.1 Hardness of nonconvex optimization in the oracle model
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}(g)$ be any deterministic algorithm which takes as input any function $g: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$
conclusions: there exists an objective function $\mathfrak{f}: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ that is 1-Lipschitz, with 8-Lipschitz gradient
nodes.statement_short: Any deterministic oracle algorithm needs 2^d oracle calls to find a 1/(2e)-global minimizer of some 1-Lipschitz function with 8-Lipschitz gradient.
nodes.label: thm:hardness_deterministic

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem B.1
nodes.statement:
We will use the probablistic method.  Let $Z$ be a uniform random point on the ball $B(0,6)$. 

 Consider the candidate function $\mathfrak{\hat{\mathfrak{f}}}(x) = -\psi(x - Z)$, and let $\phi(x) = 0$ for all $x$. 
 
  Then $\hat{\mathfrak{f}}$ has all its derivatives equal to zero outside of the ball $B(Z,1)$. 
  
   Therefore, $\mathcal{A}(\phi)$ and  $\mathcal{A}(\hat{\mathfrak{f}})$ are exactly the same algorithm up to the point when $\mathcal{A}(\phi)$ makes an oracle query for a point in the ball $B(Z,1)$.

Let $\mathcal{I}$ be the number of oracle calls until the algorithm $\mathcal{A}(\phi)$ queries a point in $B(Z,1)$. 

 We will show that $\mathcal{I} \geq 2^d$ with probability at least $\frac{1}{2^d}$. 
 
  Let $x_1,\ldots, x_{\tau}$ be the sequence of points at which algorithm $\mathcal{A}(\phi)$ makes its first $x_{\tau}$ oracle calls, where $\tau := \min(2^d-1, \mathcal{I})$.  Let $x_{\tau+1}:= \tilde{x}(\phi)$ be the output of the algorithm. 
  
   Then for all $j>0$ we have
   
\begin{equs} \mathbb{P}(x_j \in B(Z,1)) \leq \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(B(0,1))}{\mathrm{Vol}(B(0,5))}= \frac{1}{5^d}.
\end{equs}

Hence,

\begin{equs} \mathbb{P}(x_j \notin B(Z,1) \forall i \in [\tau+1] ) \geq 1- 2^d \times  \frac{1}{5^d} -1 \geq 1- \frac{1}{2^d}.
\end{equs}

Therefore, Inequality \eqref{eq:hardness2} implies, with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{2^d}$, that we have both $\mathcal{I} \geq \frac{1}{2^d}$ and $\tilde{x}(\phi) = x_{\tau+1} \notin B(Z,1)$. 

 Therefore, with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{2^d}$, $\mathcal{A}(\phi)$ and  $\mathcal{A}(\hat{\mathfrak{f}})$ are exactly the same algorithm for their first $2^d$ oracle calls (or until both algorithms terminate) and $\tilde{x}(\phi)\notin B(Z,1)$. 
 
  Therefore, we have that, if $\mathcal{A}(\hat{\mathfrak{f}})$ outputs a point before it makes $2^d +1$ oracle calls, this point must be $\tilde{x}(\hat{\mathfrak{f}}) = \tilde{x}(\phi) \notin  B(Z,1)$ with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{2^d}$.

Therefore, since all the global $\varepsilon$-minimizers of $\mathfrak{f}$ are in the ball $B(Z,1)$, we must have that, with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{2^d}$, algorithm $\mathcal{A}(\hat{\mathfrak{f}})$  does not output an $\varepsilon$-minimizer of $\hat{\mathfrak{f}}$ before it makes $2^d +1$ oracle calls.  Since the probability of this event is nonzero, there must exist a function $\mathfrak{f}$ for which the algorithm $\mathcal{A}(\mathfrak{f})$ must make at least $2^d$ oracle calls to find an $\varepsilon$-global minimizer of $\mathfrak{f}$ for $\varepsilon = \frac{1}{e}$.

nodes.name: Hardness of finding exact local minima
nodes.statement: One can also show that finding an exact local minimum can require a number of function calls which is exponential in the dimension $d$, using roughly the same ideas as in the proof  Theorem \ref{thm:hardness_deterministic}.  Consider the class of functions $f(x) = \mathrm{sigmoid}(x[1]) - 10\psi(x + c)$. for some $c \in \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\|c\| \leq 10$.  This function has only one exact local minimum, and this exact local minimum is always in a ball $B(c,1)$ of radius $1$ around $c$.  But, for this class of functions, $c$ can be anywhere inside a ball $B(0,10)$ of radius 10 centered at the origin, and the only way to ``find" this ball using a gradient or function oracle is if one calls this oracle inside the radius 1 ball $B(c)$.  Then any algorithm will require at least $\frac{\mathrm{vol}(B(0,10)}{\mathrm{vol}(B(c,1)} = 10^d$ function or gradient evaluations to find a point within a distance of $1$ of the exact local minimum of $f$.

nodes.statement_short: Finding an exact local minimum can need 10^d oracle calls, by hiding a bump in a ball of radius 10.
nodes.label: local_minimum_hardness

nodes.name: Hardness of optimizing bounded Lipschitz ReLU networks
nodes.statement:
When the objective function one wants to optimize is a neural network of Lipschtiz RELUs, \cite{goel2017reliably} show that optimizing the weights of this neural network is at least as hard as the {\em Learning Sparse Parity with Noise} problem. 

 Specifically, consider the class of depth-2 neural networks with $k$ RELUs with the restriction $\|w\|_1 \leq 2k$ on the weight vector and taking inputs on $\{0,1\}^n$. \cite{goel2017reliably}  show that the problem of finding such weights that globally optimize a $2k$-Lipschitz objective function of the outputs of the Neural network within error $\varepsilon = \omega(1)$ is at least as hard as the {\em Learning Sparse Parity with Noise} problem for parity functions on size $k$ subsets of the vertices of the $n$-cube $\{0,1\}^n$.
nodes.section: B.2 Hardness of optimizing bounded Lipschitz RELUs
nodes.statement_short: Globally optimizing a depth-2 network of k Lipschitz ReLUs is at least as hard as learning sparse parities with noise.

nodes.name: Hardness of learning sparse parities with noise
nodes.statement: This problem is conjectured \cite{goel2017reliably} to require time $n^{\Omega(k)}$ to solve, based on the best currently available bounds \cite{blum2003noise, valiant2012finding}.

conclusions: to require time $n^{\Omega(k)}$ to solve

nodes.name: Gradient bound
nodes.statement:
Therefore, since $|\psi | \leq b$,
\begin{equs}
\|\nabla_x  \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)}\left [\min(\psi(x  + \sigma \zeta),  \psi(x^\star)) \right] \|&\leq \int_{\zeta \in \mathbb{R}^d: \|x - \zeta\| \leq \delta} 0  \times \left \|\nabla_x \frac{1}{\sigma^d} \phi(\frac{1}{\sigma}(x - \zeta))\right\|  \, \,\mathrm{d} \zeta\\
&\qquad +  \int_{\zeta \in \mathbb{R}^d: \|x - \zeta\| > \delta} b \times \left \|\nabla_x \frac{1}{\sigma^d} \phi(\frac{1}{\sigma}(x - \zeta)) \right\|  \, \,\mathrm{d} \zeta\\

& = 0 + b \times \int_{\zeta \in \mathbb{R}^d: \|x - \zeta\| > \delta} \frac{\|\zeta\|}{\sigma^3 \sqrt{2\pi}} e^{- \frac{\|\zeta\|^2}{2 \sigma^2}} \, \,\mathrm{d} \zeta\\

&\leq b \times \frac{\varepsilon}{b} = \varepsilon.
\end{equs}

\noindent
This completes the proof of the left-hand Inequality \eqref{eq_local_lemma2}.
nodes.statement_short: The truncated integrand vanishes in the ball, giving gradient <= eps.

nodes.name: Hessian bound
nodes.statement:
By a similar reasoning, we also have that
\begin{equs} \|\nabla^2_x \mathbb{E}_{\zeta \sim N(0,I_d)}\left [\min(\psi(x  + \sigma \zeta),  \psi(x^\star)) \right] \|_{\mathrm{op}}&\leq \int_{\zeta \in \mathbb{R}^d: \|x - \zeta\| \leq \delta} 0  \times \left \|\nabla^2_x\frac{1}{\sigma^d} \phi(\frac{1}{\sigma}(x - \zeta))\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}  \, \,\mathrm{d} \zeta\\
&\qquad +  \int_{\zeta \in \mathbb{R}^d: \|x - \zeta\| > \delta} b \times \left \|\nabla^2_x\frac{1}{\sigma^d} \phi(\frac{1}{\sigma}(x - \zeta)) \right\|_{\mathrm{op}}  \, \,\mathrm{d} \zeta\\

& = 0 + b \times \int_{\zeta \in \mathbb{R}^d: \|x - \zeta\| > \delta} \left (\frac{\|\zeta\|^2}{\sigma^5 \sqrt{2\pi}} +  \frac{1}{\sigma^3 \sqrt{2 \pi}} \right) e^{- \frac{\|\zeta\|^2}{2 \sigma^2}} \, \,\mathrm{d} \zeta\\

&\leq b \times \frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon}}{b} = \sqrt{\varepsilon}.
\end{equs}
nodes.statement_short: Same bound for the Hessian operator norm.
